title: Verdant Hospitality ops call jotter
content:
Meeting: Discovery call — Verdant Hospitality (ops + infra)
Date: 2026-01-15 11:00 PST (45m) — notes captured live + cleaned up 2026-01-18
Attendees: 
- Verdant: Asha Patel (Head of Ops), Mark Liao (Infra/Cloud), Rhea Gomez (Data & Analytics)
- Redwood: Priya Natarajan (SE), Marco Díaz (Solutions Eng)

One-line summary:
Customer runs a mid-size boutique hotel chain (~120 properties, EMEA+NA) and wants an LLM assistant for front-desk and operations (guest messaging triage, incident response triage, standard policy recs). Looking for private deployment options due to GDPR + PCI-adjacent data. Interested in a quick POC (4–6 weeks) to validate latency and rule-out hallucinations.

Background / context:
- Existing tech: Azure tenancy (EU region for EMEA), central ops platform built on Kubernetes (AKS). They currently use Dialogflow for simple intents; want richer, context-aware responses that can reference property-specific data (amenities, local policies).
- Data sensitivity: guest PII & payment reference tokens stored in separate PCI vault; they want LLM to never see raw card numbers and prefer KMS integration + strict audit logs.
- Org constraints: security review required for any 3rd-party hosted inference; preferred route is Redwood Private (VPC) or an on-prem appliance in their EU data center.

Primary use cases discussed:
1) Guest messaging bot: 80% triage, 20% escalate to human. Must provide citations to property policies, not hallucinate booking IDs.
2) Ops runbook assistant: internal staff ask for incident remediation steps, standard operating procedures; lower latency tolerance but high accuracy required.
3) Post-stay summarization for Ops (digest of incidents per day).

Non-functional requirements (from call):
- Latency SLOs: 90th pct <= 450ms for short turn 32-token responses; 99th pct <= 900ms preferred for chat path.
- Throughput: initial pilot traffic estimate 120 reqs/min at peak across 3 properties; scale target for rollout ~1200 reqs/min across all properties (targeted Dedicated capacity).
- Data residency: EMEA data must remain in EU for all persisted artifacts; ephemeral inference can be routed to NA for performance but they prefer EU-only for pilot.
- Security: SSO via SAML/Okta, KMS integration (Azure Key Vault), audit logging to SIEM (Splunk).
- Model choices: prefer open models with fine-tuning/rlhf offboarded. Interested in smaller quantized models for cost/latency (e.g., 7B q4/8bit variants) but want Redwood to propose tradeoffs.

Gotchas / red flags noted live:
- They will have a legal gate: Legal will require proof that LLM outputs are not stored outside EU. Need data flow diagram for Private deployment ASAP.
- PCI-adjacent: they treat any flow that references booking/payment metadata as sensitive. Need to ensure PII scrubbing+kms annotation and that we can configure tokens/hashes at the connector layer.
- Ops SLA expectations may be stricter than pilot; need to confirm what counts as "incident" vs "expected failure" for SLA credits.
- Mark (infra) asked about GPU hardware and whether we support AMD-based nodes for private deploy — answer: we currently certify NVIDIA HW first; can discuss AMD but will be slower to certify.

Quick rough capacity calc (back-of-envelope):
- Pilot: 120 reqs/min =~ 2 req/sec. Assume avg output 64 tokens per response; token generation throughput per GPU depends on model variant; recommend dedicated small cluster: 1x A10-like node or 2x T4 equiv for redundancy.
- Rollout: 1200 reqs/min =~ 20 req/sec -> likely need 4–6 GPUs depending on batching and KV cache usage.
Note: these are approximate; recommend perf run with sample prompt set.

Success criteria for POC (proposed):
- 95% of guest messages classified and handled automatically with correct policy reference (measured by evaluation set + human review).
- Latency 90th pct <= 450ms for templated responses during pilot load test.
- No persisted guest PII leaves EU region; audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance.
- Integration proof: SSO + KMS + sample connector to their property DB.

Integration approach & POC plan (4–6 weeks):
Phase 0 (Week 0): contract + security questionnaire + NDA signed.
Phase 1 (Week 1): Environment setup (Private VPC in their EU tenant OR Redwood Private in customer-subnet). Provide data flow diagram, network requirements. Owners: Priya (Redwood), Mark (Verdant).
Phase 2 (Week 2–3): Model onboarding + prompts + sample data. Build connector that redacts card-like tokens and hashes booking ids. Provide 50 example prompts from their operations team.
Phase 3 (Week 3–4): Load/perf tests + latency tuning. Run synthetic load to reach 120 reqs/min and measure. Tune batching, KV cache, and consider quantized model if needed.
Phase 4 (Week 5–6): Human-in-the-loop review for accuracy, create failure-mode playbook, hand-off runbook for their support.

Action items / next steps (owners + tentative dates):
- Send Redwood POC checklist + security SCQ to Verdant (Priya) — due 2026-01-19 (DONE).
- Mark to share network contact + Azure tenant ID + Splunk ingest endpoint — due 2026-01-22 (pending).
- Marco to draft data flow diagram and EU-only persistence configuration for legal review — due 2026-01-25.
- Build redaction prototype (hash booking id; drop raw card tokens) — assigned to Marco/Evelyn — initial demo by 2026-01-29.
- Perf test plan with sample prompts (include 50 real-ish guest messages) — Priya to coordinate with Rhea — due 2026-02-05.

Prompts / evaluation seeds (copied from chat during call):
- "Guest: My reservation number 87912 — can I get a late checkout?" -> expected: ask for property policy, reference booking id hash, provide allowed options, escalate only if VIP or booked via third-party.
- "Staff: How do we escalate a water leak on 3rd floor?" -> expected: step-by-step runbook entry + contact info for maintenance.

Open questions to resolve (for sales + SE):
- Is Redwood Private packaging priced as a one-time appliance or subscription? Need quote range for a 6-month pilot and for annual Dedicated capacity. (Sales to provide ballpark)
- Legal wants explicit language on "no model training on customer data" for the pilot; can we add contractual clause? (Contracts)
- AMD GPU support timeline — confirm with infra eng for any near-term certification. (SE -> Infra)

Notes to self / shorthand: 
- Emphasize EU-only persistence in next email; attach a network diagram + process for KMS key rotation.
- For hallucination mitigation: propose retrieval-augmented generation with strict citation behavior + answer templates that include "source: [policy-id]".
- Consider a lightweight selective redact pass at ingestion to remove direct card numbers and PII before sending context to model (also flag to client: this reduces model context fidelity).

Follow-up email outline (to send after Mark shares Azure details):
1) Thanks + recap of call
2) Attach POC checklist + SCQ (security) + simple data flow diagram (EU-only)
3) Ask for network contact + sample dataset + Splunk endpoint
4) Propose dates for Phase1/Phase2 (Week 1 start)

Misc / artifacts to attach to POC folder:
- Security questionnaire (SCQ) template
- POC checklist + runbook template
- Redaction library prototype (node/python snippets)
- Sample prompt corpus CSV (50 rows)

—— END NOTES ——

(Keep this as my working scratchpad. Will convert to a micro-PRD once we have network + legal sign-off. If Mark pushes for AMD or on-prem racks, escalate to infra and Solutions leadership.)
